skill.name: uv-package-manager
skill.description: Guide for using the uv package manager to create Python projects, manage dependencies, pin Python versions, build virtual environments, and optimize CI workflows.
skill.summary: Use uv to manage Python dependencies, environments, lockfiles, and Python project workflows.
skill.author: ActiveInferenceInstitute

security_audit.summary: No prompt injection or hidden malicious intent was found in the reviewed skill content. Most external command findings are Markdown code fence false positives, but the skill includes remote installer commands that pipe scripts into shells and one persistent ~/.bashrc edit. Those risky examples should be replaced with verified installation steps and explicit user approval.

remediation.issue: Remote installer piped directly into sh.
remediation.suggestion: Replace pipe-to-shell installation with package manager instructions or a download, inspect, verify, then execute workflow.

remediation.issue: PowerShell installer uses Invoke-RestMethod piped to Invoke-Expression.
remediation.suggestion: Avoid irm-to-iex examples. Instruct users to download the installer, verify the source, inspect it, then run it intentionally.
Use a session-only PATH export or ask the user to manually review shell profile edits before making persistent changes.

content.value_statement: Python dependency management can be slow and inconsistent across environments. This skill guides uv workflows for project setup, virtual environments, lockfiles, and CI.
actual_capabilities: Explains when to use uv instead of pip, pip-tools, poetry, or conda.
Provides workflows for project setup, dependency changes, syncing, locking, and running tools.
Guides virtual environment creation, activation, and Python version pinning.
Shows uv patterns for CI, Docker, monorepos, pre-commit, and VS Code.
Troubleshoots PATH, cache, Python version, dependency conflict, and lockfile issues.
limitations: It does not execute commands or inspect the local environment by itself.
Installer commands require user review because some download and run remote scripts.
Placeholder package names and repository URLs must be replaced before use.
Current uv behavior should be checked against the latest official documentation.

use_cases.title: Start a Python Project
use_cases.description: Create a uv-based project plan with dependencies, dev tools, Python version pinning, and lockfile workflow.

use_cases.title: Optimize CI Builds
use_cases.description: Design repeatable CI steps that install uv, sync dependencies, run tests, and reuse cache safely.

use_cases.title: Migrate Existing Dependencies
use_cases.description: Move a project from requirements files, pip-tools, or poetry toward uv commands and lockfile practices.

prompt_templates.title: Create a New uv Project
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the uv package manager skill to plan a new Python project for [application]. Include the Python version, main dependencies, dev tools, and setup steps.

prompt_templates.title: Migrate from pip
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the uv package manager skill to migrate my project from requirements files to uv. Explain the dependency, lockfile, and virtual environment changes.

prompt_templates.title: Build a CI Workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the uv package manager skill to design a CI workflow for [project type]. Include dependency sync, cache strategy, tests, linting, and lockfile checks.

prompt_templates.title: Troubleshoot a Workspace
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the uv package manager skill to diagnose a uv workspace with dependency conflicts, multiple Python versions, and slow CI installs. Provide a safe investigation plan.

output_examples.input: I have a Python service with slow dependency installs in CI.
output_examples.output: The skill returns a uv-based CI plan with caching, frozen dependency sync, test execution, and lockfile checks.

output_examples.input: I want to migrate a requirements-based project to uv.
output_examples.output: The skill outlines migration steps, dependency grouping, lockfile creation, virtual environment setup, and compatibility notes.

output_examples.input: My team needs one workflow for local development and Docker builds.
output_examples.output: The skill compares local, CI, and container workflows and recommends consistent uv commands for each environment.

best_practices: Confirm installer sources and checksums before running installation commands.
Commit uv.lock and use frozen installs for reproducible builds.
Prefer uv run for project commands to reduce environment drift.
anti_patterns: Piping remote installer scripts directly into a shell without review.
Mixing pip, poetry, and uv changes in one project without a migration plan.
Ignoring lockfile changes after dependency updates.

faq.question: What does this skill help me do?
faq.answer: It helps plan uv workflows for Python projects, dependencies, virtual environments, lockfiles, CI, Docker, and migrations.

faq.question: Does the skill install uv automatically?
faq.answer: No. It provides guidance and command examples. Users should review installation commands before running them.

faq.question: Can it replace pip guidance?
faq.answer: It can explain uv alternatives to pip workflows, but projects may still need pip-compatible exports for some systems.

faq.question: Does it cover Python version management?
faq.answer: Yes. It describes uv commands for installing, listing, pinning, and using Python versions.

faq.question: Is it useful for CI and Docker?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes repeatable patterns for dependency sync, frozen installs, cache use, testing, and container builds.

faq.question: What should users verify before running examples?
faq.answer: Users should verify URLs, package names, repository paths, shell profile edits, and project-specific dependency constraints.
